160.body:
Existing UFC behavior can support a partial grappling identity, but it does not justify three reliable hard style classes. Generic control and submission activity show moderate persistence across nonoverlapping career blocks; significant ground activity is noisier, and escape/scramble ability remains unidentified. Conclusion: **B — PARTIAL IDENTITY IS SUPPORTABLE**.

Adds all twelve requested reports, strict-prior fighter states, separate decision/finish histories, 2018–2026 boundary/original-date/division support, fixed B3/B5 diagnostics, source feasibility and a hashed evidence manifest under `docs/data_audits/grappling_identity_competing_pathways_v1/`. The one next recommendation is a frozen nonpredictive replication of decision-only control versus all-history SUB activity at comparable TD access.

Audit head: `d0ca33c89b63edd0517ea233454a17f295ae5b2c`.

The published Git tree exactly matches the locally verified tree.

No predictive fits, F01/F02 changes, B3/B5 changes, altered PR #125 predictions, prospective outcome access, simulator implementation or model promotion. Draft only; do not merge automatically.

The independent simplified ground-pathway POC is a valid negative result: continuous fighter identity improves this mechanistic model versus population-average ground behavior, but the frozen primary model underperforms directional Arm C. No promotion is justified.
